claim: The IETF draft defines a shared robots.txt policy token in the User-Agent line to express AI-training preferences, with no new grammar.
quote: This document introduces no new directive names and no new grammar

claim: The token is __usage_ai-training.
quote: This document defines the policy token __usage_ai-training.

claim: The draft is authored by Kevin Kelley of Anthropic and is an individual draft without IETF endorsement.
quote: not endorsed by the IETF

claim: Wildcard groups do not count; a file without the token expresses no preference.
quote: wildcard groups (i.e., User-Agent: *) MUST NOT be interpreted as matching the policy token

claim: The token does not control crawling; crawler rules are separate.
quote: This policy token is not a directive for crawling behavior.

claim: AI training is defined as modifying a generative model's learned parameters (from the AIPREF vocabulary).
quote: Using an asset to modify the learned parameters of a generative AI model.

claim: Private agreements can override the signal.
quote: Private agreements MAY override preferences expressed via this mechanism.

claim: Anthropic has started implementing support and keeps its existing crawler controls.
quote: Anthropic has already started implementing support for this draft.

claim: Google will support a shared AI training control in robots.txt across multiple providers.
quote: express their AI training preferences across multiple AI providers in a single step

claim: Google will treat a token opt-out as a Google-Extended disallow unless Google-Extended is specified.
quote: Google plans to interpret that as if the publisher had disallowed Google-Extended

claim: Google aims to support the control in 2027 (crawler docs: early 2027).
quote: We aim to support this new control along with other AI providers in 2027

claim: Only sites that allow Google-Extended are eligible for Gemini grounding, so the shared opt-out has a grounding side effect at Google.
quote: Websites that specifically allow Google-Extended are eligible to appear in responses and receive clicks via grounding in Gemini Apps.

claim: Google-Extended does not affect Google Search inclusion or ranking.
quote: Google-Extended does not impact a site's inclusion in Google Search

claim: Microsoft will honor the preferences starting Feb 1, 2027.
quote: Starting February 1, 2027, Microsoft will honor the new preferences as it crawls.

claim: Microsoft treats training and grounding separately; neither affects traditional Bing search eligibility.
quote: Training and grounding are independent preferences.

claim: OpenAI will honor the shared signal in the coming months, with existing crawler controls kept (secondary only; primary post returned 403).
quote: will roll out in the coming months, with implementation details to follow

claim: The signal covers training only, not web search, AI answers, or user-triggered requests.
quote: says nothing about web search, AI answers, or user-triggered requests

claim: Critic Nate Hake says the draft exempts user-initiated actions and is not settled at the IETF.
quote: basically exempts the preferences from applying to anything a user does

claim: Hake: significant disputes remain at the IETF level.
quote: it's not actually done at the ietf level -- and some significant areas of dispute remain

claim: Commentary notes the signal has no enforcement mechanism.
quote: no enforcement teeth
